title: Getting started with estbanr
text: ESTBAN (Estatística Bancária Mensal por Município) monthly balance-sheet statistic Brazilian Central Bank publishes every bank branch country, aggregated accounting document 4500. row carries balances 45 accounts (verbetes) COSIF chart accounts, credit operations (160), financing (162), rural credit (163), savings deposits (420) time deposits (432), one branch (agencia files) one institution one municipality (municipio files). monthly, municipal goes back 1988, ESTBAN public source credit deposits municipal level Brazil. also large, awkward download: one national CSV per month, ;-separated, Latin-1 encoded, two title lines file names changed years. estbanr takes care mechanics:

title: Getting started with estbanr
code: # From CRAN (when available): install.packages("estbanr")  # Development version: # remotes::install_github("StrategicProjects/estbanr")

title: Non-reports and imputation
text: ESTBAN assembled Central Bank monthly returns institution. bank’s return make file. bank still listed, every branch every account equal zero. documented case Banco Santander January March 2025: three consecutive months zero whole country, back normal April. non-report, zero balance sheet. Summing rows municipal series makes credit deposits fall bank’s share three months jump back, model fed series reads real shock. Re-downloading help: published files .

title: Non-reports and imputation
text: estban_flag_nonreport() marks every row institution-month whose accounts sum zero across whole table. wider table, safer test: one dormant branch can legitimately zero everywhere, bank zeros every city state (country) reported. Let us build three-month series extract shipped package make one bank vanish February:
code: library(estbanr)  f  <- system.file("extdata", "202401_ESTBAN_AG_sample.CSV", package = "estbanr") m1 <- estban_read(f, uf = "PE") verb <- grep("^verbete_", names(m1))  m2 <- m1; m2$ref <- 202402L; m2[, verb] <- m2[, verb] * 1.05 m3 <- m1; m3$ref <- 202403L; m3[, verb] <- m3[, verb] * 1.10 m2[m2$cnpj == "60746948", verb] <- 0          # Bradesco: nothing in February  x <- rbind(m1, m2, m3) flagged <- estban_flag_nonreport(x) unique(flagged[flagged$nonreport, c("nome_instituicao", "ref")]) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   nome_instituicao     ref #>   <chr>              <int> #> 1 BCO BRADESCO S.A. 202402

title: Non-reports and imputation
text: estban_impute_nonreport() treats flagged institution-months missing, collapses branches one row per institution municipality, fills interior gaps linear interpolation along (institution, municipality, account) series. Gaps start end series left NA: bank stopped reporting last month stays missing file revised, instead invented. February now midpoint January March, imputed column says many accounts filled row (45).
code: imp <- estban_impute_nonreport(x) #> ℹ 1 institution-month flagged as non-report; interpolating interior gaps. v <- "verbete_160_operacoes_de_credito" imp[imp$cnpj == "60746948" & imp$municipio == "CARUARU", c("ref", v, "imputed")] #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>      ref verbete_160_operacoes_de_credito imputed #>    <int>                            <dbl>   <int> #> 1 202401                        23110341        0 #> 2 202402                        24265858.      45 #> 3 202403                        25421375.       0

title: Non-reports and imputation
text: estban_by_municipality() runs imputation default. Compare credit series Caruaru without : Without treatment, February short whole credit missing bank (small share city, total even fall, exactly makes error hard spot); , February sits January March .
code: raw <- estban_by_municipality(x, impute = FALSE) fix <- estban_by_municipality(x) #> ℹ 1 institution-month flagged as non-report; interpolating interior gaps. data.frame(   ref     = raw$ref[raw$municipio == "CARUARU"],   raw     = raw[[v]][raw$municipio == "CARUARU"],   imputed = fix[[v]][fix$municipio == "CARUARU"] ) #>      ref        raw    imputed #> 1 202401 3368237459 3368237459 #> 2 202402 3512383474 3536649332 #> 3 202403 3705061205 3705061205

Genuine exits. bank closed branches municipality shows zero . edge gap left NA design, closure happened two reported months window (reopened later), interpolation bridge . Look imputed column nonreport trusting long bridge. Balance identities. Interpolated accounts longer add exactly totals (verbete_399_total_do_ativo, verbete_899_total_do_passivo), account interpolated separately. Recompute totals components need identity.

title: estbanr: ESTBAN monthly banking statistics by municipality from R
text: bank’s monthly return make ESTBAN file: bank still listed, every account equal zero every branch country (Banco Santander, January March 2025, documented case). Summed municipal series looks like credit collapse followed rebound. estban_flag_nonreport() finds institution-months estban_impute_nonreport() fills interior gaps linear interpolation, never extrapolating edges. See vignette("nonreport-imputation").

title: Impute non-reported institution-months — estban_impute_nonreport
code: # Three months of a two-bank, one-city extract, with bank B zeroed in the # middle month. See vignette("nonreport-imputation") for the full story. f <- system.file("extdata", "202401_ESTBAN_AG_sample.CSV", package = "estbanr") m1 <- estban_read(f, uf = "PE") m2 <- m1; m2$ref <- 202402L m3 <- m1; m3$ref <- 202403L verb <- grep("^verbete_", names(m1)) m2[m2$cnpj == "60746948", verb] <- 0          # Bradesco "vanishes" in February m3[, verb] <- m3[, verb] * 1.10               # and everything grows 10% by March x <- rbind(m1, m2, m3) imp <- estban_impute_nonreport(x) #> ℹ 1 institution-month flagged as non-report; interpolating interior gaps. imp[imp$cnpj == "60746948" & imp$municipio == "CARUARU",     c("ref", "verbete_160_operacoes_de_credito", "imputed")] #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>      ref verbete_160_operacoes_de_credito imputed #>    <int>                            <dbl>   <int> #> 1 202401                        23110341        0 #> 2 202402                        24265858.      45 #> 3 202403                        25421375.       0

what: estbanr: Access 'ESTBAN' Monthly Banking Statistics by Municipality from the Brazilian Central Bank — estbanr-package
title: estbanr: Access 'ESTBAN' Monthly Banking Statistics by Municipality from the Brazilian Central Bank — estbanr-package
text: Download, read tidy 'ESTBAN' ('Estatistica Bancaria Mensal por Municipio'), monthly banking statistics published Brazilian Central Bank ('Banco Central Brasil') every bank branch municipality Brazil, balance-sheet accounts ('verbetes' 'COSIF' chart accounts) credit operations, deposits savings. Files fetched official site https://www.bcb.gov.br/estatisticas/estatisticabancariamunicipios idempotent local cache, read 'Latin-1' CSV layout tibbles, optionally filtered state, aggregated municipality. Includes tools detect impute institution-month non-reports (institution present file every account equal zero), otherwise mistaken zero balances.

title: estbanr 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Download read. estban_url() knows file-name variants Central Bank used; estban_download() tries order, unzips keeps idempotent cache (estban_cache_dir(): argument, ESTBANR_CACHE_DIR, option, tempdir()); estban_read() parses Latin-1, ;-separated files typed tibbles snake_case names optional state filter; estban_fetch() range months. Layout dictionary. estban_columns() estban_verbetes() describe columns file families (agencia, municipio) parse COSIF account codes, including combined columns. Non-reports. estban_flag_nonreport() detects institution-months published every account zero; estban_impute_nonreport() interpolates interior gaps per institution, municipality account without extrapolating; estban_by_municipality() aggregates municipality wide long form, imputing default. small real extract (four municipalities PE PB, January 2024) ships inst/extdata/ examples, tests vignettes run offline.
